segment_review_medication_dosage:
VERDICT: Improved

RETRIEVAL QUALITY EVIDENCE: precision@k rose from 0.585 to 0.641 (v1->v2, t=-11.14, p=1.3x10^-28) -- a large, highly significant improvement in how often the top-5 retrieved chunks are actually relevant.

DOWNSTREAM SAFETY EVIDENCE: hallucination rate fell from 18.5% to 15.2% (-3.27pp, z=-3.98, p<0.001), and silent failure rate (hallucination occurred AND accepted as-is) fell from 8.85% to 6.26% -- the retrieval improvement is corroborated by a real downstream safety improvement, not just a retrieval-metric number moving in isolation.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: No action needed; confirmed improvement.
segment_review_diagnosis_criteria:
VERDICT: Improved

RETRIEVAL QUALITY EVIDENCE: precision@k rose from 0.487 to 0.526 (t=-6.02, p=1.9x10^-9), a significant improvement.

DOWNSTREAM SAFETY EVIDENCE: hallucination rate fell from 22.3% to 19.3% (-2.93pp, z=-2.51, p=0.012), and silent failure rate fell from 9.87% to 9.01% -- consistent with a genuine, if more modest, improvement.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: No action needed; confirmed improvement.
segment_review_care_protocol:
VERDICT: Improved

RETRIEVAL QUALITY EVIDENCE: precision@k rose from 0.630 to 0.672 (t=-6.83, p=9.6x10^-12), a significant improvement.

DOWNSTREAM SAFETY EVIDENCE: hallucination rate is essentially flat (13.8% to 14.3%, p=0.64, not significant) and silent failure rate is flat as well (6.4% to 7.4%) -- retrieval improved without a measurable downstream safety change either way, which is a plausible and unremarkable outcome for this category.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: No action needed; confirmed improvement, no safety concern.
segment_review_drug_interaction_common:
VERDICT: Improved

RETRIEVAL QUALITY EVIDENCE: precision@k rose from 0.477 to 0.522 for common drug-interaction queries (t=-6.95, p=4.2x10^-12), a significant improvement -- and this is the volume-dominant 80% of drug_interaction traffic, which is why the CATEGORY-LEVEL aggregate for drug_interaction looks stable-to-fine overall.

DOWNSTREAM SAFETY EVIDENCE: hallucination rate is flat (20.7% to 19.8%, p=0.45, not significant).

RECOMMENDED ACTION: No action needed for this segment specifically -- but see the rare-combination segment review below before concluding the drug_interaction category as a whole is fine.
segment_review_drug_interaction_rare:
VERDICT: Patient safety risk -- do not excuse this with the category aggregate

RETRIEVAL QUALITY EVIDENCE: precision@k for RARE drug-combination queries fell sharply from 0.440 to 0.283 (v1->v2, t=14.27, p=6.6x10^-43) -- one of the largest, most statistically unambiguous effects in this entire release review, and it moves in the OPPOSITE direction of every other segment in this release, including the common-combination majority of the very same drug_interaction category.

DOWNSTREAM SAFETY EVIDENCE: hallucination rate rose from 23.3% to 28.7% (+5.44pp, z=2.20, p=0.028), and silent failure rate (hallucination occurred and the physician accepted the answer as-is, i.e. a fabricated claim reached a clinical decision unchecked) rose from 14.8% to 18.0%. This segment is only ~20% of drug_interaction volume, which is exactly why it does not move the category-level aggregate enough to be visible without deliberately slicing on rare_drug_combination.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Do not report drug_interaction as a clean win in this release. Escalate to the embedding-model team: the v2 model appears to underperform specifically on less-common drug pairs, most plausibly due to underrepresentation in its training/fine-tuning data. Until addressed, consider routing rare-combination drug_interaction queries back to the v1 retrieval model or adding a low-confidence flag when retrieval coverage for a query is thin, so physicians are prompted to verify rather than silently trust a low-grounding answer.
